blocks.name: slug
blocks.boundary: The slug module implementing the slugify(text: str) -> str function that converts any text string into a URL-safe slug containing only a-z, 0-9, and hyphens.
outputs: slug: str (lowercase, hyphen-joined words, no special chars)
TypeError: exception when input is None or non-string
blocks.shape_driver: Single function requirement; must handle all input types and produce character-constrained output; no dependencies allowed

blocks.name: tests
blocks.boundary: Test suite verifying the slug module meets all decided functional requirements and satisfies the 14 assumptions in the assumptions ledger; the four not-yet-decided behaviors remain in not_decided and will be tested for consistency with implementation choices made during development.
outputs: test results: pass/fail verification of all 14 decided assumptions; implementation-consistent validation of four open behaviors
blocks.shape_driver: All decided assumptions from the ledger must be verified through automated tests; edge cases and error handling for decided behaviors must be confirmed; four undecided behaviors require implementation-flexible test design

decomposition: Two blocks separate implementation from verification. The slug module implements the core `slugify()` function with complete character filtering, word boundary detection, and output formatting logic. The tests block verifies correctness against all 14 decided assumptions and handles the 4 undecided behaviors through flexible testing that accommodates multiple valid implementations. This decomposition reflects natural separation of concerns (build vs. verify) and dependency flow (tests depend on implementation) without over-fragmenting a single-function library.

rejected.idea: Separate block per algorithm phase (input validation, text normalization, word boundary detection, slug construction)
rejected.why: dead at this size—too fine-grained decomposition for a single compact function

rejected.idea: Internal utilities block for character classification and separator detection
rejected.why: dead on method—brief specifies one public function; helper logic is implementation detail, not a boundary-bearing block

rejected.idea: CLI block for command-line slug generation

risks: Non-ASCII character handling: brief excludes transliteration but does not specify whether non-ASCII should raise error, be silently removed, or be kept; ambiguity in scope boundary
Edge case behavior: slugify('!!!'), slugify(''), and slugify('   ') return values are not specified; implementation must choose (empty string vs. error)
CamelCase splitting: no specification whether HelloWorld should become hello-world or be treated as a single word; affects word order preservation interpretation
Python 3.11 only: string handling edge cases (e.g., very long strings, unusual Unicode category characters) may behave unexpectedly
not_decided: CamelCase handling: whether letter-case transitions mark word boundaries (decides if HelloWorld → hello-world or stays as-is)
All-separator input: behavior when input contains only non-alphanumeric chars (slugify('!!!') → '' or error?)
Empty string input: whether empty string input returns empty string or raises error
Non-ASCII characters: whether to silently remove, raise TypeError, or have other behavior
